title: Basic 9 · Image × mask (Multiply)
summary: Make a circular mask with the MO (Model image) node, then multiply it by a Camera image to keep only the central disk.

steps.title: Build masking with multiplication
steps.body:
The most practical use of multiply is **image × mask**. The mask is a binary (or soft-coefficient) image whose value is 1 where you want to keep content and 0 where you want to discard it, so:

  **output = image × mask** → 1 regions pass through, 0 regions become 0.

Basic 4's Circular mask does exactly this internally. Here we build it explicitly: generate a circular mask with **MO (Model image)** and multiply it against a Camera image via `arith.binop` with op=mul.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Camera** (128×128). This is the image we'll mask.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.camera` shows its image.

steps.title: Drop MO (Model image)
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Model image** (`data.mo`) — the mask-generator node. Its `kind` dropdown offers circle / gaussian / soft_circle / rectangle / ring and more.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.mo` shows its mask image.

steps.title: Click MO
steps.body: Click MO. The Inspector reveals `nx` / `ny` (output size), `kind`, `density` (value inside the shape), `radius`, and more. Defaults: `kind=circle`, `density=1`, `radius=20`, `nx=ny=128`.

steps.title: Set nx to 128
steps.body: Enter **128** in `nx` — matches Camera's size (both operands must share shape for multiply).

steps.title: Set radius to 40
steps.body: Enter **40** in `radius`. A radius-40 disk gets value **1** inside and **0** outside — this binary mask decides the keep/kill regions for the multiply step.

steps.title: Drop the Arithmetic node
steps.body: From Arithmetic, drag **Arithmetic · a ∘ b** (`arith.binop`) — the multiply happens here.

steps.title: Wire Camera → a
steps.body: Drag from Camera's `image` output to `arith.binop.a`. Convention: the image being masked goes on `a`.

steps.title: Wire MO → b
steps.body: Drag from MO's `image` output to `arith.binop.b`. The mask goes on `b`.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The default `op=add` gives Camera + Mask — a baseline before we switch to multiply.

steps.title: Click Arithmetic
steps.body: Click Arithmetic. Default `op` is `add`; switch to `mul`.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The MO circular mask is multiplied pixel-wise with Camera: only the inside of the disk keeps the camera content, everything outside becomes 0 (black).

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
**Play with it — change the mask shape:**
  - MO `kind` = **`soft_circle`** → cosine-rolled boundary, best for suppressing Fourier-domain ringing.
  - `kind` = **`gaussian`** → a Gaussian window (centre-weighted window function).
  - `kind` = **`ring`** + `radius` / `width` → annular mask (same effect as a Basic-4 mask with the centre punched out).
  - `kind` = **`rectangle`** + `width` / `height` → rectangular crop.
  - `density` = 0.5 → softly dim the whole image by 50 %.

**Takeaway:** MO + binop lets you design arbitrary mask shapes — Basic 4's Circular mask is convenient but shape-locked. In real cryo-EM, a soft-edged circular or elliptical mask from MO is routinely multiplied with particles.

That completes the arith trio (`add` / `sub` / `mul`) — same `arith.binop` node, only `op` changes. Next: **Basic 10 · Apply a filter** moves us into frequency filtering.
